message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the **presence of a mane** in adult males. The genes that control mane development are located on the X chromosome, and the allele that produces a full mane is dominant over the allele that results in a smaller or absent mane. This means that if a male lion inherits the dominant allele from either parent, it will develop a mane.
